Answer: B
Reason: The CT images demonstrate a markedly dilated main pulmonary artery (indicated by the measurement line in Figure 1a) and right ventricular enlargement, which are hallmark signs of pulmonary hypertension. This condition explains the exertional dyspnea and is characterized radiographically by prominent central pulmonary arteries with tapering or "pruning" of the peripheral vessels due to increased vascular resistance.
